subject_matter: Meaning — the concept space of meaning in philosophical discourse: sense, reference, use, difference, significance
source: Frege, 'On Sense and Reference' (1892); Husserl, Ideas I (noema); Russell, 'On Denoting' (1905); Wittgenstein, Philosophical Investigations §43; Austin, How to Do Things with Words (1962); Saussure, Course in General Linguistics (1916); Derrida, Of Grammatology (1967), 'Différance' (1968); Dilthey, The Formation of the Historical World; Heidegger, Being and Time §32; Gadamer, Truth and Method (1960)

signature.meaning: the first determines the second (sense determines reference; difference determines sense)
the first is constituted by the second (meaning constituted by use)
the first defers the second (presence, reference, significance postponed in the play of differences)
the first is that upon which the second is projected (significance as the Woraufhin of understanding)
the first holds independently of the second
